question: In a logic circuit, two inputs A and B are applied to an AND gate, and the output of the AND gate is connected to the input of a NOT gate. If the inputs A and B are both at logic 0, what will be the output of the entire circuit?
solution:
The correct answer is __1**(Undefined)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this logic circuit__, two inputs A and B are applied to an AND gate.
 
• The output of the AND gate is connected to the input of a NOT gate.
 
• If inputs A and B are both at logic 0, the output of the AND gate will also be 0.
 
• The NOT gate will then invert this output to produce a logic level of 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **AND Gate:**

 
 
• A logic gate that outputs a logic level of 1 only if all its inputs are 1.
 
• For inputs A = 0 and B = 0, the output is 0.
 
 
 
• **NOT Gate:**
 
 
• The NOT gate inverts its input: if the input is 0, it outputs 1, and vice versa.
 
• In this case, the input to the NOT gate is 0, so the output will be 1.
 
 
 
• **Logic Circuit Output:**
 
 
• The entire circuit produces a final output of 1 when both inputs A and B are 0.
